action: Begin scanning the pancreas in a longitudinal (long) section.
interpretation: Establish the initial long-axis view of the pancreas.

action: Survey the longitudinal plane to identify key landmarks. Note the position of adjacent structures.
interpretation: Visualize the spine, abdominal aorta, pancreas, and left lobe of the liver. Identify adjacent bowel loops which often obscure the pancreas.

action: Utilize the longitudinal view to optimize system physics. Place the focal zone directly at the level of the pancreas. Optimize the depth setting.
interpretation: Ensure the focus is in the right place.

action: Adjust global Gain. Adjust Time Gain Compensation (TGC) sliders.
interpretation: Verify that gain and TGC are set correctly for the tissue characteristics.
Transition from longitudinal view to the classical transverse pancreas view.
Visualize the pancreatic head, the body, and part of the tail.

action: Return to long section to confirm window. Rock the probe cephalad and caudad (up and down). Instruct patient to change respiration. Rotate probe 90 degrees back to transverse.
interpretation: Ensure the pancreas is fully visualized in long section before rotating.

action: Rotate and angle the probe towards the patient's left shoulder. Increase depth.
interpretation: Target the visualization of the pancreatic tail, which requires deeper penetration.
Identify specific anatomy: Tail of the pancreas, spine, abdominal aorta, Superior Mesenteric Artery (SMA), and the splenic vein joining the portal confluence.
